A 46-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. He has type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. Current medications include metformin and lisinopril. He reports that he has adhered to his diet and medication regimen. His hemoglobin A1c is 8.6%. Insulin glargine is added to his medication regimen. Which of the following sets of changes is most likely to occur in response to this new medication?
$$$ Glycolysis %%% Glycogenesis %%% Lipolysis %%% Gluconeogenesis $$$?

enhanced_information: Insulin glargine activates insulin receptors leading to increased GLUT4 translocation and enhanced glucose uptake by cells. This results in decreased blood glucose levels, stimulation of glycogen synthesis, inhibition of lipolysis, and reduced gluconeogenesis. Therefore, the most likely set of changes in response to insulin glargine is an increase in glycogenesis and a decrease in lipolysis and gluconeogenesis (option opb: ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓).
analysis: Insulin glargine is a long-acting insulin that helps lower blood glucose levels by promoting glucose uptake in tissues and inhibiting hepatic glucose production. It enhances glycolysis and glycogenesis while inhibiting lipolysis and gluconeogenesis. Therefore, the expected changes with the addition of insulin glargine would be an increase in glycolysis and glycogenesis, and a decrease in lipolysis and gluconeogenesis.
